newsitem.title: UK: TIACA offers air cargo improvement proposals.
newsitem.headline: TIACA offers air cargo improvement proposals.

text.p: The International Air Cargo Association (TIACA) said it has suggested actions to improve airfreight industry performance.
Its industry affairs committee said in a statement received here that these proposed actions focus primarily on factors that will affect the growth and development of the air cargo industry.

In the 'Ress Report', prepared by TIACA chairman Jean-Alain Ress, the committee identifies customer satisfaction and performance standards as main objectives for all industry players, in order to increase customer confidence and attract new markets.

Ress, general manager of cargo services for Aeroports de Paris, calls for establishing global quality and performance standards among the various industry participants -- shippers, forwarders, airports, airlines, customs, brokers and others.
He also emphasises the need for the industry to enforce timeframes within which all operations must be completed.
To improve ground "fluidity" and reduce transit times, the Ress Report suggests eliminating peak-hour congestion by providing more attractive tariffs during off-peak periods.
Ress also calls for the reduction of multiple handling processes and unnecessary paperwork, coupled with better use of technology and logistics, to reduce transit times.

Stressing the importance of customer and carrier communication, Ress suggests improved feedback and shipments and improving the quality of ground handling through professional training in seminars and educational programmes.

The report lists customer satisfaction/performance standards among the key industry issues controlled by the industry's operators, along with tariff structures, booking and tracking, multi-modality and communications.
